family.story: a poor family in Chennai, in an informal settlement, mother and father, 1 older sibling

milestones.question: mitu is six. school costs money the family barely has. do the parents send them?
milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2032 · the first day of school. the family chose send them to school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are seven. what do you do in the afternoons?

options.label: read and study with an older cousin
help the family earn: carry water, mind the stall
play outside with the street kids

milestones.reasoning: the family needed every hand
outcome: closer to the family, less time for school
milestones.caption: 2033 · afternoons after school. the family chose help the family earn. the parents decided: the family needed every hand

milestones.question: the family goes to worship every week. what do they raise mitu with?

options.label: raise them in the faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: it is how they were raised
outcome: grew up inside a faith community
milestones.caption: 2035 · the family faith. the family chose raise them in the faith and its community. the parents decided: it is how they were raised

milestones.question: you are twelve. the family needs money. do you stay in school?

options.label: leave school and work to feed the family
work in the day, study at night

milestones.reasoning: the family needed every hand
outcome: earned a little, school ended at twelve
milestones.caption: 2038 · stayed in school or left. the family chose leave school and work to feed the family. the parents decided: the family needed every hand

milestones.question: you are sixteen. friends pass around cigarettes and drink. what do you do?

options.label: say no and join a sports team

milestones.reasoning: i don't want to get into trouble and i have a lot on my mind with school and saving up for something special.
milestones.thought: today was hard but i didn't smoke or drink. i'm glad i said no, even if it felt weird at first.
milestones.caption: 2042 · cigarettes, drink, or sport. chose say no and go home, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

milestones.question: you are 17, with 6 years of school, in Chennai. the streets are tense. which path?

options.label: work the family farm or stall

milestones.reasoning: can't afford nursing or teaching right now. trade is too long-term for savings. farm work isn't needed here. factory job pays more than market helper.
milestones.thought: today was tough, but i made it to the factory and saved a few rupees. mitu.
milestones.caption: 2044 · the path after school. chose take the factory job now over work the family farm or stall, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken the

milestones.question: you have a little free time. where does it go?

options.label: keep up with close friends, every week
join a community group (faith, sport, neighborhood)

milestones.reasoning: i need the emotional support from my friends right now. we can share stories and laugh together.
milestones.thought: sitting with nusrat and talking about our hopes for the future always makes me feel better.
milestones.caption: 2045 · who to spend time with. chose keep up with close friends over work extra shifts, because an earlier life learned: always keep at least one close friend through every busy decade. they will be there when you need t

milestones.question: you are 24. wages here are low. unrest is high. stay in Chennai or go?
milestones.reasoning: stay in chennai, near family. money is tight and unrest is high, moving would cost too much and expose me to more risk.
milestones.thought: today was just another day of work, prayers, and hoping things stay steady.
milestones.caption: 2050 · move or stay. chose stay in chennai, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you met someone you like. what do you do?

options.label: wait, focus on yourself for now

milestones.reasoning: i need to save more and focus on my family first.
milestones.thought: today was just another day at the factory, but i saved a little more. rahim’s arthritis is getting worse, so i’ll get him some medicine tomorrow.
milestones.caption: 2052 · love. chose wait over commit, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: you lost your job as undefined.

options.label: take any work you can find
lean on family while you look

milestones.reasoning: i need to find something to do quickly to cover my expenses. retraining would take too much time and money i don't have right now. lean on family is nice but they are already struggling.
milestones.thought: needed to take that cleaning job even though it's not what i want, just to get some cash in hand.
milestones.caption: 2053 · laid off. chose take any work you can find, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you children?
milestones.reasoning: i need to save more and feel stronger first. my mom needs help, and i can't risk it now.
milestones.thought: today was hard, but i saved a little more. rahim's cough sounds worse; maybe he should see a doctor soon.
milestones.caption: 2054 · children. chose wait a few years over no children, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and get checkups before small problems become big ones

milestones.question: you earn about $54 a month. what do you do with it?
milestones.reasoning: i need to save for future needs. my mom and sister are getting older and might need help soon.
milestones.thought: saved a bit more this month, hoping it'll be enough if something happens with my mom or nusrat.
milestones.caption: 2055 · what to do with money. chose save a tenth every month over enjoy it now, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you are 31. your body is starting to complain.
milestones.reasoning: can't afford to lose money from not working and need all my energy for earning.
milestones.thought: another day, another dollar saved. hope i don’t get sick.
milestones.caption: 2057 · health at thirty. chose no time for that, can't afford to lose money from not working and need all my energy for earning

milestones.question: you work as day laborer. what next?

options.label: study at night for a better job
switch to work that helps people (care, teaching)
take a promotion that means cheating workers on pay

milestones.reasoning: i can barely save any money as a day laborer. training would take time and cost more in books i don't have. helping people might be rewarding but pays less. starting a business without savings is too risky. cheating workers feels wrong, even if it means better pay.
milestones.thought: another day of hard work, another step closer to the end of this month.
milestones.caption: 2063 · mid-career. chose stay put, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: a protest fills the streets of Chennai and it is turning violent. do you join?

options.label: stay home, keep the family safe
help the injured at the edges
take what you can while the shops are open

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to risk my safety and i need to save what money i have for my family.
milestones.thought: today was hard but safe. - mitu khan
milestones.caption: 2064 · the protest. chose stay home, i can't afford to risk my safety and i need to save what money i have for my family
milestones.world: in South Asia public approval collapses almost overnight: people now say out loud what they said in private

milestones.question: there is need all around you. do you give your time?

options.label: mentor young people in your trade

milestones.reasoning: i want to help others and find purpose in service.
milestones.thought: spent the day at the local food bank, feeling a bit tired but also fulfilled.
milestones.caption: 2066 · helping others. chose volunteer every week over family comes first, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: faith is everywhere here. where do you stand?

options.label: go deeper into faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: faith gives me comfort and a sense of community. i can pray more and help others who are hurting.
milestones.thought: praying with my friends feels like home now.
milestones.caption: 2069 · faith. chose go deeper into faith and its community over nothing changes, because an earlier life learned: turn grief into service for those who are hurting

milestones.question: you are 47. something feels off.
milestones.reasoning: can't afford regular checkups right now. money tight.
milestones.thought: just another day in life, nothing much to report today.
milestones.caption: 2073 · the checkup. chose ignore it, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

milestones.question: rahim died, my father. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i need to lean on my friends and family for support during this tough time. we can help each other through the grief.
milestones.thought: rahim's gone, but we're still a family, even if just me and nusrat now.
milestones.caption: 2076 · grief. chose lean on friends and family over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: an old friend writes after years of silence.

options.label: write back, meet up, keep it going

milestones.reasoning: too many responsibilities right now. maybe later when things settle down.
milestones.thought: had to work extra today. feels good to finish early and rest a bit before anything else.
milestones.caption: 2077 · old friends. chose too busy, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: fatima is getting frail.

options.label: take them into your home and care for them

milestones.reasoning: i can’t afford to take her in, and paying for care is too expensive. visiting when i can at least lets me stay connected.
milestones.thought: rahim’s gone, but nusrat’s still out there somewhere; maybe we’ll meet again someday.
milestones.caption: 2081 · aging parents. chose visit when you can over take them into your home and care for them, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: you lost your job as undefined.

options.label: take any work you can find
lean on family while you look

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to lose any more savings, and retraining would cost too much time. my family will help me while i find my footing.
milestones.thought: just another day of not working, but at least mum and nusrat are here for me today.
outcome: family carried them until a new job came
milestones.caption: 2087 · laid off. chose lean on family while you look over take any work you can find, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: fatima died, my mother. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i need to lean on them now more than ever. they are my support and i can rely on their trust.
milestones.thought: fatima is gone but her memory lives in their warmth. - mitu khan
milestones.caption: 2089 · grief. chose lean on friends and family over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: you are 64, with $454 saved. retire?

options.label: work part time, keep a purpose

milestones.reasoning: i need the money and i still want to be useful. retiring now would be too much to give up.
milestones.thought: today was hard but i helped a few kids learn their abcs. rahim and fatima would be proud of me for not giving up.
milestones.caption: 2090 · retirement. chose work part time over retire, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: where do you want to grow old?

options.label: stay in the neighborhood, among friends

milestones.reasoning: i have friends here and i trust them. they've been there for me during tough times. moving near my nieces would be nice, but it's not as important as staying close to those who know me well.
milestones.thought: today was quiet, spent with old friends. rahim and fatima would be proud of the little community we built together.
milestones.caption: 2096 · where to grow old. chose stay in the neighborhood, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: what do you want to leave behind?

options.label: write down the family story for the grandchildren

milestones.reasoning: even though i'm short on money, i can still offer my time and support to help others in need. it's a way to keep busy and stay connected with the community.
milestones.thought: today was just another day of walking to the volunteer center and helping those who needed it. rahim would be proud.
milestones.caption: 2100 · what to leave behind. chose volunteer while the body allows over rest, because an earlier life learned: turn grief into service for those who are hurting

milestones.question: you are eighty. the walking group meets every morning.
milestones.reasoning: i'm feeling a bit off today and it's just too much to push myself.
milestones.thought: just needed some quiet time for myself. - mitu khan
milestones.caption: 2106 · staying active. chose stay home, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: nusrat died. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: helping others who lost someone might give me a sense of purpose and distract from my grief.
milestones.thought: nusrat’s gone, but maybe i can help another soul find comfort where i couldn’t.
milestones.caption: 2108 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: turn grief into service for those who are hurting

milestones.question: the last years. what matters now?

options.label: make peace with anyone you are estranged from
give your savings to the grandchildren now

milestones.reasoning: money is tight and i need to focus on my health and what brings me peace.
milestones.thought: just another quiet day, praying for strength and comfort in solitude.
milestones.caption: 2114 · the last years. chose a quiet life, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and get checkups before small problems become big ones
